It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. The nearby {{ill|Shinobugaoka Station|eo|Stacio Shinobugaoka|it|Stazione di Shinobugaoka|ja|忍ケ丘駅|ko|시노부가오카역|nl|Station Shinobugaoka|ur|شینوبوگاوکا اسٹیشن|zh|忍丘站|qid=Q855840}} is named after the shrine. It is sometimes read as “Ninryō-jinja.” {{nihongo|'''Shinobugaoka Shrine'''|忍陵神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Kawachi Province|be|Каваты (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Kawachi|ckb|پارێزگای کاواچی|cs|Provincie Kawači|de|Provinz Kawachi|es|Provincia de Kawachi|fa|ولایت کاواچی|fr|Province de Kawachi|gl|Provincia de Kawachi|hak|Kawachi-koet|id|Provinsi Kawachi|it|Kawachi (provincia)|ja|河内国|ko|가와치국|lt|Kavačio žemė|nl|Kawachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Kawachi|ru|Кавати (провинция)|simple|Kawachi Province|sk|Kawači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Кавачи|tr|Kawachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Каваті|zh|河內國|zh_min_nan|Kawati-kok|zh_yue|河內國|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}}.

It stands on the mound of '''{{ill|Shinobugaoka Kofun|ja|忍岡古墳|qid=Q11490749}}''', and the site is also said to have held '''Okayama Castle''' in the Sengoku period.

== History ==
Shinobugaoka Shrine was renamed in Meiji 44 after Tsuhoko Shrine merged two nearby shrines. Tsuhoko Shrine’s original deities were {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|az|Fucivara no Kamatari|be|Фудзівара-но Каматары|ca|Nakatomi no Kamatari|de|Fujiwara no Kamatari|es|Fujiwara no Kamatari|fa|فوجیوارا نو کاماتاری|fi|Fujiwara no Kamatari|fr|Fujiwara no Kamatari|hr|Fujiwara no Kamatari|hy|Ֆուձիվարա նո Կամատարի|id|Fujiwara no Kamatari|it|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|ko|나카토미노 카마타리|nl|Fujiwara no Kamatari|pl|Kamatari Fujiwara|pt|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ru|Фудзивара-но Каматари|sh|Fujiwara no Kamatari|sv|Fujiwara no Kamatari|sw|Fujiwara no Kamatari|th|ฟูจิวาระ โนะ คามาตาริ|tr|Fujiwara no Kamatari|uk|Накатомі но Каматарі|vi|Fujiwara no Kamatari|zh|藤原鎌足|zh_min_nan|Huziwara no Kamatari|qid=Q433995}}, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|simple|Kumano Gongen|zh|熊野權現|qid=Q11568925|lt=Kumano Ōkami}}.

The founding date of Tsuhoko Shrine is unknown, but it is seen as originally worshiping the ancestral deity of the local ancient clan {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsuhoko clan}}, later taking {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997}} as ujigami. Until the Edo period it was called Shingū Daigongen, with a tradition that {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=En no Gyōja}} founded it in the time of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ar|الإمبراطور تيمو|arz|الامبراطور تيمو|azb|تمو|ca|Tenmu|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر تێنمو|cs|Temmu|de|Temmu|eo|Temmu|es|Tenmu Tennō|fa|امپراتور تنمو|fr|Tenmu|hak|Tenmu Thiên-fòng|he|טמו, קיסר יפן|hu|Tenmu japán császár|id|Kaisar Tenmu|it|Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|ka|ტენმუ|ko|덴무 천황|la|Tenmu (imperator)|nl|Tenmu|pl|Tenmu|pt|Tenmu|ru|Император Тэмму|sh|Car Temmu|simple|Emperor Tenmu|sl|Cesar Tenmu|su|Kaisar Temmu|sv|Tenmu|th|จักรพรรดิเท็มมุ|tl|Emperador Temmu|tr|Temmu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Темму|vi|Thiên hoàng Tenmu|yo|Emperor Temmu|zh|天武天皇|zh_min_nan|Tenmu Thian-hông|zh_yue|天武天皇|qid=Q335181}}. As {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumano worship}} spread in the Heian period, {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|熊野権現|simple|Kumano Gongen|zh|熊野權現|qid=Q11568925|lt=Kumano Ōkami}} was merged in. Its original site was at Akayama in Tsuboi, Okayama village, south of the current site, but in the Edo period it moved to the current site and merged Kamatari-sha (deity: Fujiwara no Kamatari) that had been here. After victory it came to be called '''Okachiyama''' (“victory mountain”) as an auspicious place, but most remains were destroyed and little can now be seen.
